rule.description: The buyer picks any revealed bid; it need not be the cheapest. Logs can show the choice was allowed, not that it was the best one. V2 enforces the budget on-chain; on V1 this tool enforces it after the fact.

revealSet.algorithm: d0 = bytes32(0); d(i) = keccak256(abi.encode(d(i-1), bidder, amount, commitment)), over reveals in (blockNumber, logIndex) order

sealing.amount: Hidden until the bidder reveals: only a salted hash is on-chain. Public from the reveal onward, for ever. A bid never revealed stays hidden.
sealing.identity: NOT hidden. The bidder's address is public from the first commitment, as are the time of the bid and any replacements.
sealing.proposal: Encrypted in the browser; only ciphertext is on IPFS. The key is published at reveal, so a revealed proposal is readable by anyone, for ever. Size and upload time are not hidden.

limitations: This report covers procedure, not merit: the buyer's choice among allowed bids is a judgement that logs cannot prove right or wrong.
Identity is an address. Logs cannot show that two addresses are unrelated, so collusion or a buyer bidding through another account stays invisible.
Evidence comes from one RPC endpoint. A dishonest RPC could serve false data; compare another endpoint or your own node where one exists.
Eligibility requirements live in the off-chain tender metadata and are not checked.
